text.p: Top Mexican beer-maker Grupo Modelo posted another impressive period in the third quarter this year, with exports booming and cash flows running strong, analysts said.
Modelo's nine-month net profit fell to 836.34 million pesos from 914.83 million during the year-ago period -- a decent result considering Mexico's weak economy, analysts said.

Sales revenues were up 6.9 percent in the third quarter over the same period last year, buoyed by a domestic sales volume increase of 13 percent and an export increase of 30.6 percent, said Isabel Rueda of the Interacciones brokerage.
Beer prices decreased in real terms as Modelo and its main competitor Fomento Economico Mexicano SA de CV, Femsa, have kept from raising prices since the second quarter.
But analysts said the overall health of Modelo is so good that lower net profits, revenues, gross profits and operating income were not much of a concern.
The company, which has no debt, is sitting on 2.287 billion pesos in cash, down from 3.420 bilion a year ago as Modelo has paid cash to build a new megaplant in the north-central state of Zacatecas.
The plant, due to come on line next year, will help solve distribution problems, particularly for exports, and help meet increased demand.
Analysts said Modelo was a particularly good buy considering the shaky status of the Mexican stock exchange and the peso.
"With the peso decreasing against the dollar, that's why people love Modelo whenever there's a black cloud on the horizon," said Thomas Mobille of Robert Fleming in Brazil.
Laura Ehrlich of Paribas in New York shared the rosy outlook for Modelo.
"We are saying as a house that Mexican stocks could be in for a rough go of it in the next quarter. If so, Modelo is the best defensive play," Ehrlich said. "Everything is so good with the company."
